ledger.claim: The driver's arrival on this trip is a driver-pressed BUTTON marker (trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker = BUTTON), not a platform-confirmed GPS_AUTO arrival, so POL-NS-12 - the clause that lets the platform's own full-resolution geofence measurement and its wait_timer_started / wait_timer_expired events establish arrival and the service of the waiting period independently of the exported trace - is expressly unavailable here. The whole charge must therefore be carried by the exported device trace and must satisfy POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-05 on that trace alone; no platform measurement corroborates the arrival event, the in-geofence position or the dwell.

The charge is only just made out on the arithmetic, and the rider asks that every element of it be found on the trace rather than assumed. The longest qualifying in-geofence run is 490 seconds (first qualifying fix 21:20:00 to the 21:28:10 cancellation, 50 qualifying fixes), against the 480-second free waiting period in force for this AIRPORT trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 480); the trace's own derived shortfall is -10 seconds, a single sampling interval of surplus. The dwell is measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 21:20:00, which is five seconds before the driver's own arrival event at 21:20:05 (dwell_start_offset_sec = 5.0), so on the driver's own arrival event the dwell is 485 seconds. On a surplus of one or two samples the qualifying run itself is the whole case: the run must be genuinely continuous and every fix in it must be accuracy-clean under POL-NS-02's 25 m filter before limb (b) and limb (c) of POL-NS-01 are treated as satisfied, and it is not enough that the driver held the bay for a period that only just crosses the line.

I do not press POL-NS-04 and I do not stretch the rider's silence into anything it is not. Limb (a) of POL-NS-04 requires a rider message in the waiting window, and this chat log contains none: all four entries are the platform's 21:20:06 arrival notice (read at 21:20:45), the driver's two messages and the driver's one unanswered voice call. POL-NS-11 does not open either, because the rider's track is present rather than absent and affirmatively fails limb (c) of POL-NS-04 - all 54 rider fixes lie roughly 1,202 to 1,211 m from the pickup pin, outside the 200 m AIRPORT presence radius, with 0 qualifying fixes. The rider's point is narrower and is this: his silence is not a limb of POL-NS-01. Every condition that clause imposes - the driver's arrival event, his in-geofence position, his continuous dwell, and the reason code on the termination - is a condition on the driver's conduct, and none of them is supplied by the rider failing to type. Whether the $6.00 stands turns on the driver's own evidence, not on the rider's conduct.

The trip record carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 21:20:05, and the GPS trace places him inside the pickup geofence before it: the first qualifying in-geofence fix is at 21:20:00, there are 50 qualifying fixes inside the 150 m AIRPORT arrival radius set by POL-NS-02, and the driver's track came as close as 21.3 m to the pickup pin. POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) are satisfied on complete, full-weight telemetry, and the POL-NS-02 proximity test is met many times over its three-consecutive-fix threshold.

The driver held position inside the arrival radius for a single continuous run of 490 seconds, from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 21:20:00 to the 21:28:10 cancellation — 10 seconds more than the 480-second free waiting period in force for this AIRPORT pickup under trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, which is the period POL-NS-01(c) requires. The dwell is measured from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not from the arrival tap, exactly as limb (c) directs, and the measured shortfall is minus 10 seconds, so POL-NS-06's premature-cancellation refund is not engaged.

The arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05. The 'arrived' event at 21:20:05 sits 5 seconds after the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 21:20:00 (dwell_start_offset_sec 5.0), with the driver stationary inside the radius and nowhere near POL-NS-05's 300 m distance or 15 km/h motion triggers. The waiting clock therefore runs from the record's own arrival, and no recomputation shortens the dwell.

The trip was terminated by the driver at 21:28:10 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises — which is 10 seconds after the required 480-second dwell elapsed at 21:28:00. The record shows no boarding event, no started_at and no actual_distance_km, so limb (d) holds: the rider never appeared.

This is not a wrong-entrance case and POL-NS-03's refund does not arise on these facts: the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the 150 m AIRPORT arrival radius, his track at one point closing to 21.3 m of the pin, so there is no 'stationary outside the radius but within 400 m' state of affairs for POL-NS-03 to decide. POL-NS-01 limb (b) is not displaced.

The charge is the correct amount and reconciles. fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee is SGD 6.00, which is exactly platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd for this trip, so there is no mismatch for POL-NS-08(d) to treat as a fare defect; payment_status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the fee is properly the net figure for the zone and vehicle tier in force.

POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full, and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, the driver is entitled under POL-NS-07 to 80 percent of the SGD 6.00 fee, that is SGD 4.80. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the absolute threshold of 4, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 120 is 0.008, far below the 0.08 rate threshold, so both limbs of the check fail and compensation is paid rather than withheld.

Because compensation is payable, the outcome this case produces is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd carrying the same SGD 4.80 figure under POL-GEN-03's single exception; the fee itself stands as charged, which POL-NS-07 expresses as NO_ACTION on the fee. NO_ACTION is not the ruling value here.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider. Limb (a) fails because the chat log's four messages are one system arrival notice and three driver messages — the rider never sent a locating or coordinating message at all; and limb (b) fails because the driver did not merely chat, he placed an in-app voice call at 21:24:05 lasting 25 seconds, recorded unanswered in trip_record.in_app_calls, before terminating the trip at 21:28:10.

Limb (c) of POL-NS-04 is affirmatively failed on admissible fixes rather than being undecidable: the rider track carries 54 fixes, every one of them at zero speed and between 1,202 m and 1,211 m from the pickup pin, so rider_qualifying_fix_count inside the 200 m AIRPORT rider-presence radius is 0 across the whole waiting window. The rider's account of looking everywhere at the pick-up area for a silver Camry is contradicted by the rider's own device.

The driver performed exactly what the platform expects at an airport kerb and what earns the fee: an in-app message at 21:20:25 naming 'T1 arrival bay 3' and a silver Camry, a second message at 21:23:05 asking whether the rider was coming, and a voice call at 21:24:05. Both messages were read by the rider (read_at 21:20:45 and 21:23:35) and neither was answered, which matches the driver's account that he messaged twice, called once and the rider never appeared; wait_time_min of 8.1 on the trip record matches his statement of 'over eight minutes'.

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00401-01 is MISSING — admissibility status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, because no advisory covers Airport Boulevard in this window — so POL-NS-06(i)'s summing of separate in-geofence intervals is unavailable to the driver, and I disclose that rather than dressing the absence as support. The driver does not need that limb: his 490-second dwell is one unbroken run, so the fee stands without any accumulation.

The 180-second post-match grace in POL-NS-10(a) is a rider-cancellation protection and cannot help here: the rider cancelled nothing — trip_record shows cancelled_by DRIVER, status CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER, at 21:28:10, some 17 minutes 20 seconds after the 21:10:50 acceptance — so no grace-based refund arises, and there is no scheduled_at on the record for POL-NS-10(b) to work with.

The rider's length of custom and the delayed bag at the belt are not grounds of decision. POL-GEN-01 permits only the nine enumerated profile fields to ground a finding, and account_age_days (700), lifetime_trips (240) and rating (4.78) are context only; nothing in the rider profile, and nothing in a delayed-baggage explanation, bears on whether the driver arrived inside the radius, held it for the required 480 seconds and waited out a rider who never came.

ledger.claim: No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is present, so this case is decidable on the record. Every artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0; the trace carries 105 fixes at a 10-second cadence with no gaps at all (max_gap_sec 0.0); the chat log's 4 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count of 4 with no msg_id gap and no truncation; no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 with disputes_with_counterparty_90d 0 on both profiles, so POL-NS-09(b), (c) and (d) are all out.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — this is a NO_SHOW_CHARGE dispute over the SGD 6.00 cancellation fee charged when the driver ended the trip at Changi Airport Terminal 1 Arrival Pick-up Bay 3 on 16 Aug 2026. The fee stands, and the driver is paid SGD 4.80.

For the driver: all four POL-NS-01 conditions hold. (a) The trip record carries your 'arrived' event at 21:20:05. (b) The GPS trace places you inside the 150 m AIRPORT arrival radius before it, at the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 21:20:00 — 50 qualifying fixes, closest approach 21.3 m to the pin — so POL-NS-02's three-consecutive-fix proximity test is met. (c) You held that geofence for one continuous run of 490 seconds, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix (not from the arrival tap), which is 10 seconds more than the 480-second free waiting period in force for this AIRPORT pickup (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 480). (d) You terminated at 21:28:10 — at or after the required dwell elapsed at 21:28:00 — under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes limb (d) recognises, with no boarding event and no started_at. POL-NS-05 is not engaged: at the arrival marker you were stationary inside the geofence, not more than 300 m out and not travelling at 15 km/h or above, so the waiting clock is not recomputed. POL-NS-03 does not apply — your stationary fixes were inside the arrival radius, not in the wrong-entrance band, so POL-NS-02's inside-radius branch governs and limb (b) is satisfied. POL-NS-06 gives no refund because there is no shortfall, and POL-NS-10 does not apply because the rider did not cancel — you did. POL-NS-07 therefore fixes your compensation at 80% of the SGD 6.00 fee = SGD 4.80, the anti-farming check being clear (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d = 1, below the absolute threshold of 4, and 1 ÷ 120 completed trips = 0.008, below the 0.08 rate threshold). Under POL-GEN-03 a case producing this outcome is ruled DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd carrying the same SGD 4.80; the fee itself stands as charged, which POL-NS-07 expresses as NO_ACTION on the fee.

For the rider: I have read your account — the 13-hour flight, the delayed bag, your custom since 2021 and your request for an apology — but none of it can decide this dispute. POL-GEN-01 makes account_age_days (700), lifetime_trips (240) and rating (4.78) context only, and a delayed bag does not bear on the conditions the fee depends on. Your two legal points are accepted but do not change the outcome. You are right that POL-NS-12 is unavailable: the arrival was a driver-pressed BUTTON marker, not a platform GPS_AUTO arrival, so the charge must rest on the exported device trace alone — and it does: 105 fixes at a 10-second cadence, full coverage and a maximum gap of 0.0 s, carrying the arrival and the 490-second in-geofence run. You are also right that the surplus over the minimum is a single 10-second interval, and that POL-NS-01's limbs are conditions on the driver rather than on your silence; but a dwell one interval over the line is still over the line, and the trace satisfies every limb. POL-NS-04 cannot help you: limb (a) requires at least one locating or coordinating message from you in the waiting window and the chat log contains none (its four entries are the platform's arrival notice, the driver's two messages and one unanswered voice call), so the clause never opens; POL-NS-11 does not open either, because your track is present and fails rather than being undecidable. Your own device recorded 54 fixes, none inside the 200 m airport rider-presence radius (they sit 1,202–1,211 m from the pin), so the record does not corroborate that you reached the bay.

The record is internally consistent on arrival, dwell and rider presence, and no artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08 (no clock skew — the arrival marker is 5 seconds from the nearest fix; no sampling gap; the chat log's 4 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count; the SGD 6.00 fare line reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd), so there is no POL-NS-09 escalation ground and no down-weighting. The artifacts carrying the deciding facts are complete at weight 1.0, hence confidence 0.95. No clause produces a referral. The amount moved, SGD 4.80, is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold in POL-GEN-05 and executes on issue. Either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
